clue.text: Seafood and a lot of gammon

indicators.note: a lot of, not all of, the word for nonsense is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: gammon is old slang for nonsense, as is baloney

explanation.surface: A diner orders a seafood starter and a big slice of gammon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gammon' looks like ham on the menu, but it is old slang for nonsense; 'lot of' means most of that word, not all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea mollusc prized as a delicacy.

clue.text: Law suit resulting from engagement

definitions.meaning: a legal case brought in court
an engagement is a battle or military clash

explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests marriage, but here means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal proceeding brought against someone, and also a military clash or fight.

clue.text: Alpine snowdrop?

parts.note: read not as a flower but as a drop, or fall, of snow down a mountain in the Alps

explanation.walkthrough: A snowdrop is a white spring flower; here it means snow dropping down an Alpine slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountainside is literally snow dropping in the Alps.

clue.text: Herb loves embracing wicked princess

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the two letters for love wrap round the princess

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, and loves gives two
Regan is one of King Lear's two cruel daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Romantic affairs entangle a wicked princess with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is a scheming daughter in Shakespeare's King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic plant used in cooking, also called wild marjoram.

clue.text: The Misses Doolittle and March meet the Queen

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion
Beth March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: Two fictional young ladies are presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like a month, but it is the family in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II was reigning when this puzzle was set.

clue.text: Representative of city involved with unfinished plan

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the words that follow are mixed together
unfinished says the word plan loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a town council tangled in a half-drafted plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts PLAN to PLA; 'involved' mixes CITY with PLA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something representative of a class is a characteristic, standard example of it.

clue.text: A shot in the arm working during a spasm

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the word for working goes inside the spasm

parts.note: a tic is a spasm of a muscle
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: An injection takes effect in the middle of a muscle cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative, something that gives a boost like a stimulating injection.

clue.text: Where one may find a maid with the usual sullen look

definitions.text: Where one may find a maid

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard
to lour is to frown or look sullen

explanation.surface: A housemaid wears her habitual scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlourmaid was a servant who waited at table and served in a house's sitting room.

clue.text: Sort of pin, say, a short surplice needed

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a cotter pin is a split pin used to fasten parts

explanation.surface: A churchman needs a pin to fasten his short vestment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the R of the pin's name is silent, so it is pronounced like the vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short white vestment worn over a cassock in church.

clue.text: Society begins, we hear, with such charity

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken, so a phrase that is pronounced the same is needed

parts.note: society begins with a capital, or large, S

explanation.surface: A charitable society is launched with great generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society begins' is read literally: the word starts with a large S, and 'large S' said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, a form of liberality.

clue.text: Kean, for example, reading a West End production

indicators.note: End points to the final letter of West
a production is a staging, here of a fresh arrangement of the letters before it

explanation.surface: The famous actor Edmund Kean gives a reading in a London West End theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like the London theatre district, but 'End' only takes the last letter of West, T. 'production' rearranges READING, A and T. Edmund Kean was a great 19th-century English actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean was celebrated for tragic roles such as Shylock and Richard III, a classic example of a tragic actor.

clue.text: Distributor requires one to go round in a car

definitions.text: Distributor requires one to go round in a car

parts.words: Distributor requires one to go round in a car
parts.note: the ignition distributor of a car engine contains a spinning arm that turns round to send current to each plug

explanation.surface: A delivery firm needs someone to drive round in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributor' suggests a delivery business; it is the ignition part of a petrol engine, whose spinning arm turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning arm inside a car's ignition distributor is the part that revolves to route current.

clue.text: So-called beach in Nebraska

definitions.meaning: a code name given to a landing beach in Normandy on D-Day, 1944
the largest city in the US state of Nebraska

explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' signals a name given rather than a real place name: the beach was named by the Allied planners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allies code-named a Normandy landing beach after the Nebraska city, which is the state's biggest.

clue.text: Roads in Alaska

definitions.meaning: roads, or a roadstead, is sheltered water where ships may lie at anchor
the largest city in the US state of Alaska

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roads' looks like highways, but in nautical use it means a safe place for ships to moor, as in Hampton Roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place for ships is called roads; the Alaskan city takes its name from the same kind of harbour.

clue.text: Block with barracks a very short distance away

parts.note: to block a road is to close it
barracks are soldiers' quarters

explanation.surface: A housing block with an army barracks just next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes fighting or living at very small range, right next to one another.

clue.text: Wilde's description of hunted animal is impossible to swallow

definitions.meaning: Oscar Wilde called fox hunting the unspeakable in full pursuit of the inedible

explanation.walkthrough: Wilde's quip in A Woman of No Importance describes the fox, the hunted animal, this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be eaten is inedible.

clue.text: A killing performance

definitions.meaning: a carrying out of a death sentence
the carrying out or playing of a task or piece of music

explanation.walkthrough: 'A killing performance' reads as a sensational show.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a condemned prisoner to death, and also the way a piece or a plan is carried out.

clue.text: Running over in accident before a turning, for example

indicators.note: before says the word for accident comes first

parts.note: a spill is a fall or accident, as from a horse

indicators.note: turning says the abbreviation for for example is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A crash happens just before a bend in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses only the abbreviation beside it; 'before' puts the accident first. 'Running over' is the noun sense, an overflow.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that overflows its container is the overflow.

clue.text: The one real paper designed for the art-lover

indicators.note: designed means put together to a plan, so the letters of the preceding words are freshly arranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A newspaper devoted entirely to art is laid out for a gallery-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges THE, I and REAL PAPER together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Victorian brotherhood of painters such as Rossetti and Millais is a devotee of that art movement.

clue.text: A toxin, perhaps, disguised in neat gin

indicators.note: disguised says the letters are hidden in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Poison is concealed in a glass of undiluted gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as a toxin that triggers the body to make antibodies is an example.

clue.text: Elected by their constituents, what do those who succeed do?

definitions.text: what do those who succeed do?

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: constituents are the parts of something, so the letters of their are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Politicians voted in by their voters wonder what winners do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters; it rearranges THEIR into HERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title is to take it over as heir, so successors come into an estate.

clue.text: Faithfully keep a present daughter brought in

indicators.note: brought in says the daughter's letter is placed inside the other words

parts.note: someone present is here

explanation.surface: A gift is faithfully kept when the daughter brings it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it means here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to a rule or promise is to follow it faithfully.

clue.text: Leaves when it's time to retire

definitions.meaning: to light out is slang for departing hurriedly, so someone who leaves does this
the call at bedtime in a dormitory or barracks for all lamps to be switched off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a noun about foliage; it is a verb meaning departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for departing in haste, and the bedtime order for lamps to be switched off in barracks.

clue.text: Nanny, perhaps, holding right money

indicators.note: holding says the goat's letters wrap round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a nanny is a female goat

explanation.surface: A children's nurse keeps hold of the correct cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny' looks like a child's nurse; it is a female goat. A GROAT was an old English silver fourpenny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The groat was an old English silver coin worth fourpence.

clue.text: Anything at all tough has to be cooked

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with, as accounts are cooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough cut of meat needs thorough cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: An old form of aught, meaning anything whatever.

clue.text: Beagle, perhaps, can get badger

definitions.meaning: a beagle is one kind of hunting dog
to badger is to pester persistently

explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' looks like the animal a dog might chase; it is the verb meaning harass.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a breed of hunting dog, and to pester someone relentlessly is to harass them.

clue.text: Covering full length of a pine

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A tall tree stretching right along a stretch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To go all the way down something from end to end is to travel its length.

clue.text: Some admiring a bard in elegant coat

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Admirers of a poet wear a stylish coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gabardine is a raincoat made from a tightly woven twill cloth.

clue.text: Former partner given money by court vanished

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A former spouse, handed a payout by the judge, disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely is gone for good, like the dodo.

clue.text: Understanding note on duplication of medical specialities

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across entry, so the note follows the repeated letters
duplication says the abbreviation for the medical department is written twice

parts.note: ENT stands for ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A hospital memo on overlap between departments shows good understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplication of' doubles ENT; 'on' places the note E after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, is a mutual understanding.
